title: Benton Street tenant displacement and deferrals
subtitle: Also: Thaler Avenue school land exchange, Bloomingdale townhouses, Bleams Road deferral and annual zoning by-law update.
overview: The committee spent most of the evening on a proposed mixed-use tower at Benton and St. George Streets. Many tenants and advocates spoke against the loss of 13 existing homes. The committee recommended deferring the item to the January 22, 2024 Council meeting so staff can arrange talks between the developer and tenants {{vote:m4}}. The applicant has offered four months of rent, and staff said a future rental replacement by-law would not apply to an application already in process.

The committee recommended approving a land exchange and planning changes so a new Catholic elementary school can be built at Thaler and Kinzie Avenues, with the park moved {{vote:m1}}. It also recommended zoning for stacked townhouses at 117 Bloomingdale Road North {{vote:m2}}.

A decision on 2150 Bleams Road was deferred to the December 11 Council meeting so the zoning level can be reviewed again and residents who took part are told {{vote:m3}}. The committee also recommended the annual zoning by-law update, with a change affecting 30 Sunbridge Crescent {{vote:m5}}. All of these are recommendations that Council must still consider.

decisions.item: 93-99 Benton Street and 39-43 St. George Street
decisions.detail: The committee recommended deferring the Official Plan and zoning applications for a 96-unit mixed-use building to the January 22, 2024 Council meeting so staff can facilitate talks between the developer and tenants on displacement {{vote:m4}}.

The committee recommended deferring the Official Plan and zoning applications to the December 11, 2023 Council meeting to review RES4 versus RES5 zoning and to notify residents who took part in consultation {{vote:m3}}.

The committee recommended adopting the Official Plan amendment and approving the zoning change to support a land exchange between the City and the Waterloo Catholic District School Board for a new school and a relocated park {{vote:m1}}.
The committee recommended approving the zoning change for a stacked townhouse development and adopting the Urban Design Brief to guide a later site plan application {{vote:m2}}.

The committee recommended approving the City-initiated updates to both zoning by-laws, and directed staff to prepare a map adjusting zoning at 30 Sunbridge Crescent, excluding floodplain and wetland lands {{vote:m5}}.

debate: Benton Street: delegates, including current tenants and tenant advocates, said the buildings are some of the few affordable homes left, that the tenants face a risk of homelessness, and that three or four months of rent would not cover higher market rents. Some urged the committee to vote no rather than defer.

Benton Street: the applicant's representatives said the legal minimum of three months is being offered plus one extra month, that further commitments depend on project finances, and that the applicant would meet tenants. Staff said the planned rental replacement by-law could not apply to an application already in process.

Bleams Road: staff recommended RES4 with a site-specific limit of five street townhouses, citing 6 m frontages, functionality and neighbourhood feedback. Some councillors questioned moving down from RES5 during a housing shortage and worried about precedent. Others, and staff, said compatibility does not mean identical.

Bleams Road: one councillor asked whether six townhouses could be allowed. The mayor cautioned against adding units on the fly, and another councillor noted the applicant had not been asked whether it wanted that, which led to the deferral.

Bloomingdale Road North: councillors raised traffic at the Bridge Street and Lancaster Street roundabout and asked staff to press the Region. They also asked about help for the tenant on site and Indigenous consultation. Staff said the City is still developing its consultation approach.
